title: Fix release runner selection for IP allow-list environments
outOfScope: Creating, moving, deleting, or reusing any release tag or GitHub Release.
Weakening same-SHA, rehearsal, smoke, compatibility, integrity, or public-install gates.
Changing organization IP allow-list entries, runner groups, branch protection, or CodeQL configuration.
Changing any workflow other than the release workflow or unrelated template behavior.

sources.reason: The failed rehearsal executed this workflow on ubuntu-latest and its exact-SHA dependency step calls the GitHub workflow-runs API.
Authoritative failed rehearsal log: the dependency query received HTTP 403 because the enterprise IP allow list did not permit the standard hosted runner address.
The still-open release Work Item requires a successful same-SHA rehearsal before v0.5.49 publication.
Regression coverage protects ordering and non-publication behavior for the controlled release workflow.
Its current conditional PYTHON selection explains why a fresh linked worktree falls back to an arbitrary system Ruff before quality gates can run.
Its fail-closed Ruff mismatch and documented recovery commands define the root behavior that must become deterministic at the quality entrypoint.
Maintainer guidance owns the release workflow's exact-SHA evidence and runner prerequisites.
Requires a governed corrective Work Item and fail-closed diagnosis rather than an ad-hoc retry or bypass.

riskAssessment.reason: The release workflow is a release-blocking control. Its runner choice must preserve every existing gate while allowing the GitHub API calls required by the enterprise IP allow-list policy.

reasons: The scope changes a release-blocking workflow configuration but does not publish a release; standard governance with explicit hosted rehearsal is required.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized complete governed execution. The published runner label is already configured by the organization; this Work Item only makes the release workflow select it through an explicit repository Actions variable.

preReviewWarnings: Verify the runner expression remains template-safe when no repository variable is configured.
Verify that a configured allow-listed runner is selected before the GitHub API dependency query without weakening any release gate.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: release.yml selects an optional repository Actions variable named AI_COCKPIT_RELEASE_RUNNER for its release job and retains ubuntu-latest as the template-safe fallback when that variable is unset.

make quality invokes provisioning when .venv is absent or its Ruff direct pin differs from the development manifest; provisioning installs the hash-locked development lockfile, then quality re-executes with .venv/bin/python.

Distribution guidance names AI_COCKPIT_RELEASE_RUNNER, requires an enterprise IP allow-list deployment to point it at a repository-authorized GitHub-hosted static-IP or self-hosted runner before release dispatch, and forbids a bypass.
Regression tests prove the variable/fallback runner selection and preserve existing same-SHA rehearsal and non-publication guards.

The repository variable AI_COCKPIT_RELEASE_RUNNER is set to the existing code-scanning runner label only after the Contract is ready, and the post-merge same-SHA rehearsal proves the API access and all release gates on that selected runner.
The Contract, Summary, Outcome, hosted checks, PR, merge, lifecycle closure, and continued #625 release record the fail-closed result truthfully.
guidelines: Keep the runner selection explicit, minimally scoped, and template-safe for repositories without an enterprise IP allow list.
Make locked local-toolchain provisioning deterministic and idempotent; never silently accept an arbitrary system tool version or install an unhashed dependency set.
Do not weaken or reorder any source identity, rehearsal, release evidence, tag, draft, publication, or quick-install control.
Document the external runner prerequisite in English and Japanese without exposing organization-specific IP addresses or credentials.

intent.problem: The v0.5.49 rehearsal for merged main commit 3c9dde5144965143963daeab43e131a7ca7a7179 failed before any release side effect because release.yml runs on ubuntu-latest and its required exact-SHA workflow-runs API query was rejected by the enterprise IP allow list. The PR's smoke and compatibility workflows do not issue that API call, so their green results did not expose this release-only incompatibility.
constraints: No tag, GitHub Release, asset, public installation claim, or gate bypass is allowed in this corrective Work Item.
Keep ubuntu-latest as the default for adopters who do not configure an allow-listed runner.
The configured runner label must be selected through a repository Actions variable, not hardcoded to this organization's runner name.
Fresh linked worktrees invoke deterministic .venv provisioning before quality; provisioning installs requirements-dev.lock with --require-hashes and exits nonzero on failure.
Do not retry v0.5.49 publication until this corrective PR merges and a new exact-main-SHA rehearsal succeeds.
intent.rationale: An explicit, documented, optional runner label maintains template portability while allowing enterprises with IP allow lists to route release jobs that call GitHub APIs through an approved static-IP or self-hosted runner.

declaredIntent.summary: Repair the release workflow's runner selection so an enterprise can bind its GitHub API-using release path to a repository-authorized allow-listed runner without weakening release controls or losing template portability.
